chief_complaint: Management of essential hypertension with associated obesity and obstructive sleep apnea
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 42-year-old white male with a longstanding history of obesity documented since 2010. In 2014 he was diagnosed with sleep apnea and a concurrent sleep disorder. Hypertension was identified in 2016 and is currently treated with lisinopril 10 mg daily. He reports full-time employment since 2019 but limited social contact as of 2020. No recent laboratory data (lipids, glucose, renal function) are available, and there is no documented CPAP therapy for sleep apnea. Blood pressure at the latest measurement was 132/86 mmHg (stage 1 hypertension). Overall health care utilization has been primarily wellness visits with two inpatient admissions of unspecified reason.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include dental filling loss and gingivitis (2019), prior unemployment and stress (resolved 2018-2020), reports of environmental violence (resolved 2018), and earlier full-time employment (resolved 2017). The patient also has a remote history of appendectomy (1989).
social_determinants: Limited social contact; full-time employment; higher education; white non-Hispanic male; resides in Westfield, MA; no documented smoking, alcohol, or substance use information.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: stage 1 hypertension (132/86). Obesity (BMI >=30) present but numeric value missing. Obstructive sleep apnea increases cardiovascular and metabolic risk. No lipid panel, HbA1c, or eGFR data available, limiting assessment of dyslipidemia, diabetes, and renal function. Charlson comorbidity index is 0; clinical complexity rated moderate. Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (HTN, obesity, OSA), metabolic (potential insulin resistance), respiratory (OSA), renal (potential hypertension‑related CKD), and psychosocial (limited social support).

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI numeric value missing despite obesity flag
No documentation of CPAP or other sleep apnea therapy
Only a single BP reading; trend data absent

clinical_impression: A middle-aged male with a moderate-complexity profile dominated by hypertension, obesity, and untreated obstructive sleep apnea. Current therapy is limited to low-dose lisinopril, and key risk-modifying data (lipids, glucose, renal function, sleep apnea treatment) are missing, indicating potential under-recognition and under-treatment of cardiovascular and metabolic risk.
